The quick start guide's Hardware Specifications table reads \"438.4 x 589 x 44 mm (17.26 x 23.19 x 1.73 in.)\" and the datasheet reads \"43.84 x 58.9 x 4.3 cm (17.26 x 23.19 x 1.69 in.)\". 44 mm is 1.732 in and 43.0 mm is 1.693 in, so neither is a conversion slip - the width and depth agree to the hundredth of an inch and only the height differs. THE REAR ELEVATION IS ISOTROPIC AT 44 AND NOT AT 43. Rendered from the PDF page at 600 dpi it reads 2221 x 223 px. Against 438.4 mm that is 5.0662 px/mm; against 44.0 mm the height gives 5.0682 - 0.04% apart. Against 43.0 it gives 5.1860, 2.4% out. A drawing that is square on one number and 2.4% out on the other has answered the question. 44.0 is used. THE FRONT ELEVATION IS DRAWN AT ITS OWN SCALE AGAIN, and a third one. It reads 2230 px wide - 5.0867 px/mm - against this guide's rear at 5.0662 and the AIS800-32D guide's front at 5.0536. Three drawings of one 438.4 mm face at three scales 0.7% apart, each measured on its own. Taking one axis or one face from another drawing is the error that made a Cisco power module 3.66 mm too wide, and it is avoided here by never mixing them. The ink below the face is the drop shadow and is discarded, as on the twin."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"2400 W PER SUPPLY, STATED IN BOTH DOCUMENTS, WHICH IS UNUSUAL FOR THIS LINE. The datasheet's feature list reads \"Hot-swappable, load-sharing, redundant 2400 W AC/DC PSUs\" and its ordering table names PSU-AC-2400W-F/-B and PSU-DC-2400W-F/-B as FRUs. The EXP800 and EXP100 supplies in this library carry no output rating at all because their vendor pages publish none. DRAW IS STATED TWICE AND BOTH FIGURES ARE RECORDED: \"Full loading 1600 W (100% traffic, 32 x 24 W optics)\" and \"1254 W (100% traffic, 32 x 12 W optics)\". The higher is the max. THE DATASHEET GIVES ONE PAIR OF FIGURES FOR BOTH MODELS and does not separate the OSFP build from the QSFP-DD one, so the same numbers stand here and on edgecore/ais800-32d. INPUT, from the quick start guide's specifications table: \"200-240 VAC, 50/60Hz, 15 A max. per PS\" and \"-48 - -60 VDC, 53 A max. per PS\". There is no low-line AC rating anywhere, and the guide adds that a single supply powering a fully loaded system must be on 200-240 VAC. THE PER-PORT BUDGET IS 30 W and is the datasheet's, qualified by it: \"for all 32 ports all with per-port maximum 30 W capability ... subject to total power distribution boundary and thermal considerations\"."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"A QUICK START GUIDE AND A DATASHEET, AND THEY DISAGREE ABOUT THE HEIGHT. The guide carries the Overview elevations, a System LEDs/Buttons enlargement, the FRU replacement figures, the Airflow Reversal figures and a Connect Power page that draws the DC supply's face; the datasheet carries the ordering tables, the part numbers and the power ratings. FIVE PHOTOGRAPHS ARE STAGED AND NONE OF THEM HELPS. All five are 960 x 700, which is 2.19 px/mm on a 438.4 mm face - less than half the elevation's resolution. They settle colour and nothing else. THE DATASHEET IS THE SAME DOCUMENT AS THE TWIN'S. It is titled \"AIS800-32O/AIS800-32D\" and covers both models in one ordering table; the QUICK START GUIDES are separate and each carries its own elevations, which is what makes the two walls independently measurable."},"the-drawings-are-upscales-and-that-was-checked":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE 600 DPI RENDER IS AN INTERPOLATION OF A 1.83 px/mm RASTER, and this was found late rather than assumed early. The elevations are embedded in the PDF at 836 x 118 and 832 x 108 px, so rendering the page at 600 dpi upscales them 2.8x. THE EDGE MEASUREMENTS SURVIVE. Re-running the seam detector on the EMBEDDED rear image at its native 1.8294 px/mm puts the inner fan rails at 150.3/153.6, 195.1/198.4, 238.9/243.3 and 284.8/288.1 against the upscale's 149.82/153.18, 194.82/198.18, 239.83/243.19 and 284.64/288.19 - every one within 0.5 mm, half a native pixel - and the native pitch of 44.83 against the upscale's 45.005. Averaging a vertical edge over 200 rows genuinely buys sub-pixel localisation; the closing arithmetic on the rear is the second check. WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE IS LETTERING, and two things were dropped because of it. See the fan-bay-numerals gap. A legend that is 3.7 native pixels tall is not read, it is guessed."},"the-management-cluster-is-shared-with-the-twin":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THAT WAS MEASURED ON BOTH, NOT ASSUMED. The same scan run on this device's front and on edgecore/ais800-32d's puts the two SFP28 apertures at 394.75-408.12 and 409.30-422.67 here against 394.77-408.22 and 409.21-422.47 there - 0.2 mm apart on a feature 13 mm wide, read off two separate drawings. The cluster is one CPU/BMC faceplate and both models carry it unchanged. WHAT IS IN IT. Two 25G SFP28 cages in one bezel legended `1 (up) 25G (up) 2`; a USB-C receptacle standing PORTRAIT to their right, legended SS with the USB trident; an RJ-45 management jack legended MGMT and an RJ-45 console legended CONSOLE beneath them, bezels 393.98-409.41 and 413.57-429.00 by y 20.78-33.64 against std/rj45@2's 15.8 x 13.2; and a recessed dark strip along the bottom carrying a round reset button legended RST and six lamps. THE USB IS A USB-C AND THE DATASHEET CALLS IT SOMETHING ELSE. Both documents' port lists say \"1 x USB 3.0 storage port\" with no connector type; the panel draws a tall rounded slot 3.8 x 8.8 mm with the SuperSpeed trident beside it, which is a Type-C on its side. USB 3.0 is the protocol and Type-C is the connector, so both are recorded and neither contradicts the other. std/usb-c@1 is placed `rotate: 90`. THE SFP28 LEGEND ALSO PRINTS A TRIANGLE BESIDE EACH NUMERAL - the panel reads `1 (up) 25G (up) 2` - and only the numerals and the 25G are drawn. On the 800G wall the matching triangle IS a lamp and is placed as one; here there is no window to anchor it to, so printing the glyph would assert a mark whose nature was not established. See the sfp28-and-port-lamp-positions gap."},"the-optical-wall":{"confidence":"measured","note":"FOUR BLOCKS OF FOUR STACKED COLUMNS, AND THE TWIN'S WALL IS NOT LIKE THIS. 2D template matching of one cage column across the front face finds all sixteen at 7.27, 30.67, 54.06, 77.46, 104.00, 127.39, 150.79, 174.38, 200.72, 224.31, 247.70, 271.10, 297.64, 321.03, 344.43 and 367.82. A SINGLE PERIODIC FIT TO THOSE IS WRONG - it gives 24.152 with an rms of 0.841 and a worst residual of 1.405 - because the steps are not uniform: they run 23.40, 23.39, 23.40, 26.54, 23.39, 23.40, 23.59, 26.34 and so on. Four short steps, one long, repeating. FITTING THE BLOCK MODEL INSTEAD CLOSES IT. Least squares on x = first + floor(i/4) * B + (i mod 4) * p gives first 7.225, block pitch 96.7913, in-block pitch 23.4243 - a gutter of 3.094 - with an rms of 0.051 mm and a worst residual of 0.091. Sixteen columns, four gangs of four. THE TWIN IS UNIFORM AND WAS FITTED SEPARATELY. edgecore/ais800-32d's wall takes a single 24.2410 pitch at an rms of 0.069 with no gutter at all. The two guides were measured independently and the difference is real, not a reading artefact: an OSFP cage is 23.1 mm wide against a QSFP-DD's 19.0, so this wall needs its room in blocks where that one can spread evenly. Template matching found the structure; the periodic fit would have averaged it away, which is the EXP100's autocorrelation lesson applied before the fact. EACH COLUMN IS ONE STACKED ASSEMBLY. The panel draws a single bezel per column holding the upper aperture, a thin bright perforated strip and the lower aperture, with the pair numbered `N (up) (down) N+1` on one baseline beneath it. Odd ports are the upper row and even the lower - the guide's own enlargement prints `31 (up) (down) 32` at the right-hand end and the panel prints `1 (up) (down) 2` at the left. ROWS, AND THEY ARE TIGHTER THAN THE TWIN'S. A row profile through one column puts the upper aperture at y 4.33 to 16.91 and the lower at 18.87 to 31.85 - a row pitch of 14.54 against the AIS800-32D's 18.00, and drawn openings of 12.58 and 12.98 against its 8.70. std/osfp@1's registry aperture is 13.5 tall, so seating it on a 14.54 pitch leaves the two rows 1.04 mm apart. That is what a stacked OSFP 2x1 cage is; the registry owns the aperture and the device owns the pitch, as the EXP100 records. Drawn widths are 22.4 against the registry's 23.1, the same consistent bias the twin shows at 18.3 against 19.0. THE INTER-ROW BAND IS DRAWN ON A BACKING RECT AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, as on the twin. Panel pattern decor paints only its holes, so a slot field on a dark panel is invisible; this band is BRIGHT on the hardware - here a single row of round perforations less than a millimetre tall, which is all the room an OSFP row pitch of 14.54 leaves for it - so each column gets its own light rect beneath the pattern - SIXTEEN bands, not one strip, because the band belongs to the cage assembly and stops between columns. The left and bottom fields get none, because those really are dark slots punched in the grey panel. THE WALL STARTS 2.4 MM HIGHER AND THAT COSTS THE PANEL A VENT BAND. The twin prints a row of slots at y 3.30 to 5.90, above its cages; here the cages begin at 4.33 and occupy that strip, so this face carries no top vent field. Its bottom field is correspondingly taller, starting at 37.20 where the twin's starts at 39.20."},"the-panel-is-mid-grey-and-that-is-why-the-vents-can-be-seen":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE CHASSIS COLOUR WAS CARRIED FROM ITS SIBLINGS AND IS WRONG. edgecore/exp100-32x, edgecore/exp800-16o and the rest of this line all carry '#3f4348', which nothing measured. Sampling the panel between features on the front elevation gives #626366, #737579 and #5d5d5e, and the vendor's own photograph ais800-32o-2-AIS800-32O-F.png and its 32D twin gives row medians of #676767, #696363 and #776f6d. Two independent sources, one answer: a MID grey. IT MATTERS BECAUSE PANEL PATTERN DECOR PAINTS ONLY ITS HOLES. On a near-black panel a field of dark slots is invisible, which is exactly how the first render came out - four vent fields declared and none of them legible. On the measured grey they read as they do on the drawing. The fix is the colour, not a backing rect, because these really are dark holes punched in a grey panel. THE FIELDS THEMSELVES ARE MEASURED: a vertical slot column at x 1.98-3.17 by y 6.33-38.98; two horizontal bands across the port wall at y 0.40-1.58 and 3.56-5.54; and a three-row field along the bottom from y 39.37 to 43.93, whose cells start at x 10.77 on a 3.17 pitch. THERE IS NO VENT FIELD AT THE RIGHT-HAND END. The columns from x 431 to 435 read a flat 67-69 with no structure at all; the right margin is plain metal behind the lamp strip."},"the-rear-closes-arithmetically":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SEVEN INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED SPANS SUMMING TO THE STATED WIDTH, which is the strongest check this rear has. 4.74 of chassis frame, 53.69 of PSU1, 4.73 of rail, 311.68 of fan block, 4.36 of rail, 53.70 of PSU2 and 5.50 of frame sum to 438.40. THE FAN PITCH TOOK FOUR INSTRUMENTS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM WAS RIGHT. Bay seams gave 45.05, the bails' edges 47.08, autocorrelation 45.05 and 48.80. The bails disagree because the FRU figure shows they are U-loops posed at a different angle in every bay - segmenting the salmon in the seven bays gives seven different vertical spans for seven identical parts. 2D TEMPLATE MATCHING OF THE HONEYCOMB SETTLED IT: six of the seven trays match at 60.60, 105.60, 150.81, 195.81, 285.82 and 331.02 (the seventh is under PSU2's bail), fitting 45.025 with an rms of 0.10. The tray frames read on two separate row bands then give 41.65 wide with a 3.36 mm rail, and 41.65 + 3.36 = 45.01. A POSED HANDLE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT; the part that repeats is. THE SUPPLIES ARE 53.7 AND BOTH WERE READ. PSU1 4.74-58.43 and PSU2 379.20-432.90 give 53.69 and 53.70. The first read of PSU1 gave 51.2 by taking an internal seam at 56.06 for its right frame; the symmetry and the closing sum identify which edge is which. THE MODULE HEIGHT IS MEASURED HERE, NOT BORROWED. Horizontal seams at y 1.38 and 42.04 bound both module types, giving 40.66 for the supplies and 40.6 for the trays. 40.6 is used for both. The rest of this library's Edgecore 1RU rears carry 40.0 as an estimate."},"the-sfp28-cages-have-a-lamp-each":{"confidence":"measured","note":"ONE ROUND WINDOW ABOVE EACH CAGE. The elevation puts bright blobs at x 399.92-401.30 and 414.16-415.75 by y 2.90-4.28 - centres 400.61 and 414.96, 14.35 mm apart against the cages' own 14.5 mm pitch - and the System LEDs enlargement resolves them as white domes in dark rims. The guide names them: \"SFP28 LEDs: Green (link/activity)\". Measured on the twin's elevation and confirmed present on this one, as the rest of the cluster was."},"the-system-lamps":{"confidence":"measured","note":"SIX RECTANGULAR LAMPS AND A ROUND BUTTON, ALL LEGENDED, WHICH IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THIS LINE USUALLY GIVES. The quick start guide's System LEDs/Buttons page enlarges the strip and names every one: \"LOC: Flashing Green (switch locator) DIAG: Green (OK), Red (fault) ALRM: Red (fault). FAN: Green (OK), Red (fault). PSU1/PSU2: Green (OK), Red (fault)\" and \"RST: Reset button\". THE POSITIONS ARE READ OFF THE ELEVATION AND THE SHAPE OFF THE ENLARGEMENT. A bright-run scan across the strip at y 39.0-40.2 finds seven runs: the button at 391.40-392.00 and the six lamps at 401.50-403.08, 407.04-408.62, 412.58-413.96, 418.32-419.50, 423.66-424.85 and 429.00-430.39. Their centres fit a 5.482 mm pitch. The enlargement resolves them as rounded rectangles about 2.4 times as wide as tall, each directly BELOW its legend - not the round dots this line's other 1RU switches use, and not a mixture of the two. THE LIBRARY'S NEAREST PART IS BIGGER THAN THE DRAWING. common/led-rect-sm@1 is 2.8 x 1.6 where the drawing reads 1.83 x 0.75, and common/reset-button@1 is 4.0 across where the button reads 2.5. Both are seated at the measured CENTRES rather than the measured sizes, because the library's indicator vocabulary is what a reader compares across devices. The 2.74 mm gap that remains between adjacent lamps is why the oversize is harmless here."},"the-triangles-are-printed-and-the-lamps-are-round":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THE FIRST MODEL OF THIS DEVICE HAD IT BACKWARDS. The panel prints `N (up) (down) N+1` beneath every column, and the triangles were first placed as common/led-arrow@1 lamps, which is what edgecore/exp100-32x and edgecore/exp800-16o do with the same-looking marks. THE DRAWING SAYS THEY ARE INK. The triangles are solid white, the same white and the same crispness as the numerals beside them. Every lamp on this face reads differently - a bright dome inside a dark rim - which is exactly how the six system lamps, the two SFP28 lamps and the round port lamps all render. A light pipe and a silkscreen glyph do not look alike at 5 px/mm, and these look like the numerals. SO THE ARROWS ARE SILKSCREEN and there are thirty-two of them, one per port, saying which row its number belongs to. No other device in this library prints this glyph yet. THE NUMERALS WERE ALSO TOO SMALL. They measure about 2.3 mm of cap height against the 1.3 mm font first used; 2.8 is what puts them at the drawn size."},"this-face-has-no-port-lamp-columns-and-the-twin-does":{"confidence":"measured","note":"AND THE GEOMETRY EXPLAINS IT. edgecore/ais800-32d carries four round lamps per port in the dark post to the left of each cage; there is no such post here. An OSFP aperture is 23.1 mm on a 23.424 mm in-block pitch, which leaves THREE TENTHS of a millimetre between neighbouring cages, where the twin's 19.0 mm QSFP-DD aperture on a 24.241 pitch leaves 5.2 mm. Scanning the posts for the twin's 4+4 dot pattern finds nothing, because there is nowhere for it to be. THE GUIDE STILL NAMES THE LAMPS - \"OSFP800 LEDs: Yellow (800G), Blue (400G), White (200G), Green (100G)\" - so they exist and this drawing does not resolve them. They are not drawn rather than guessed at.
